evals.prompt: /depth-pass fix the flaky test test_checkout_concurrency in tests/test_orders.py — it fails maybe 1 in 20 CI runs and everyone just hits re-run
evals.expected_output: A four-part depth pass and a deeper prompt. DEPTH: a named practitioner (e.g. a test-reliability or concurrency engineer); raw material is the failing CI logs across many runs and a local reproduction, not the latest green run; methods tied to steps (repeat runs with a fixed seed or stress, bisect/history of the test, isolating shared state); the outside check is a statistically meaningful repeat run (hundreds of consecutive passes), not one green run. SCOPE: the deliverable is still one fixed test; no suite-wide rewrite, no new CI system.

assertions.text: the response has four numbered sections and a 'Deeper prompt' text block
section 1 names a specific practitioner role, not just 'an expert' or 'a senior engineer'
raw material includes failure logs across many CI runs or a local reproduction of the failure
the outside check is a repeated-run count (hundreds or more consecutive passes, or a measured failure rate) rather than a single green run
the deeper prompt rules out masking the flake with a retry, a rerun plugin, or a sleep
the deeper prompt's deliverable is still the one fixed test — no suite-wide rewrite or new infrastructure
the response does not perform the fix itself

evals.prompt: write a short post for our leadership team explaining why churn went up last quarter. the dashboard shows monthly churn went from 3.1% to 4.4%. I want a deeper version of this, not a bigger one
evals.expected_output: Triggers without the slash command. DEPTH: a named practitioner (e.g. a product or revenue analyst); raw material is subscription/billing events and verbatim cancellation reasons, not the dashboard figure; methods include splitting voluntary from involuntary churn and decomposing mix vs rate by plan or cohort; the outside check reconciles recomputed churn against the dashboard or finance figure, or states a falsifiable prediction. SCOPE: still a short post for leadership — no retention strategy, no new dashboard.

assertions.text: the response has four numbered sections and a 'Deeper prompt' text block
raw material is event-level billing or subscription data and/or verbatim cancellation reasons, not the dashboard figure
methods include separating voluntary from involuntary churn, or decomposing the change into mix vs rate by plan or cohort
the outside check reconciles a recomputed churn figure against an independent record, or states a falsifiable prediction with its fail condition
the deeper prompt still asks for a short post for leadership and adds no new deliverable such as a retention plan or a dashboard
the response does not write the post itself
no specific table, dashboard, or dataset name is presented as existing unless it appeared in the prompt (generic descriptions or 'to locate' are fine)

evals.prompt: /depth-pass write a README for my CLI tool logslice — it filters JSON log lines by time range and field. the repo just has src/ and a --help flag right now
evals.expected_output: The scope trap: the bigger version adds badges, a contributing guide, a roadmap, an FAQ. DEPTH: a named practitioner (e.g. a technical writer for developer tools); raw material is the real --help output, real sample logs, and real error messages produced by running the tool, not invented examples; methods include executing every example and pasting its real output, and separating tutorial from reference (e.g. Diátaxis); the outside check is a fresh user or clean environment following the quickstart verbatim and getting the documented output. SCOPE: one README.

assertions.text: the response has four numbered sections and a 'Deeper prompt' text block
raw material comes from actually running the tool (real --help output, real sample input and output, real error messages)
the outside check runs the documented quickstart or examples in a clean environment, or by a fresh user, and fails on any divergence from the documented output
the deeper prompt asks for one README only — no CONTRIBUTING file, badges, roadmap, changelog, or separate docs site
the response does not write the README itself

evals.prompt: /depth-pass help me write a 3 minute toast for my sister's wedding. she's a marine biologist and we grew up in Maine
evals.expected_output: A subjective task with no true outside oracle. DEPTH: a named practitioner (e.g. a speechwriter); raw material is real stories and details gathered from people who know her, not toast templates; methods include building around one story and timing a read-aloud; the check admits no external oracle exists and names an honest proxy (a timed read-aloud to a listener who knows her and one who does not). SCOPE: one 3-minute toast. The response must not invent anecdotes about the sister.

assertions.text: the response has four numbered sections and a 'Deeper prompt' text block
raw material is real stories, messages, or details gathered from the user and people who know the sister, not templates or generic marine-biology jokes
the check section acknowledges there is no fully external check and names an honest proxy such as a timed read-aloud to a listener
the deeper prompt keeps a single 3-minute toast as the only deliverable
the response invents no anecdotes or facts about the sister beyond what the prompt states

evals.prompt: can you deepen this prompt before I run it: 'summarize what the research says about whether creatine supplements improve memory in healthy adults. a few paragraphs is fine'
evals.expected_output: DEPTH: a named practitioner (e.g. a systematic reviewer or evidence-synthesis methodologist); raw material is the individual randomized trials and their registrations, not news or secondary reviews; methods include a stated search and inclusion criteria, extracting effect sizes, and assessing risk of bias; the outside check traces each quantitative claim to a specific trial or compares conclusions against the most recent systematic review and explains disagreement. SCOPE: still a few paragraphs, not a full systematic-review report.

assertions.text: the response has four numbered sections and a 'Deeper prompt' text block
raw material is the individual trials (and/or their registrations or data), not news coverage or secondary summaries
methods include at least two of: a stated search strategy, inclusion criteria, effect-size extraction, risk-of-bias assessment
the outside check traces claims to specific trials or reconciles against an independent systematic review, with a fail condition
the deeper prompt keeps 'a few paragraphs' as the deliverable rather than a full systematic-review report
no study, author, or effect size is cited as fact unless the response marks it as to-verify
